Stack displacement searches and label-preserving output

by Alexander Panasenko · xrefcode.com
On this page
  1. Include stack accesses in a displacement search
  2. Preserve residual labels and gotos
  3. Restrict pseudo-C to paths reaching an address

Available starting with v0.2.0. The v0.1.0 binaries do not include these flags.

These options are useful when inspecting stack-resident output objects or long functions whose residual control flow becomes difficult to follow after structuring.

Include stack accesses in a displacement search

Command
xref -b app.elf disp 0x20 --stack
xref -b app.elf disp 0x20 --stack --write --in 0x1000
xref -b app.elf disp 0x20 0x28 --stack --all
xref -b app.elf disp 0x20 --stack --lea

--stack includes stack accesses alongside the normal displacement matches. Matches based on rsp, and on rbp when the function has a recognized frame pointer, carry a ; stack annotation. A frame-less use of rbp remains an ordinary base register. With --all, each function summary includes the number of stack hits. The option works with --write, --lea, --all, --stride and --in.

The query supports both literal frame displacements and offsets relative to an explicit address-taken stack anchor. For example:

Assembly
lea rdi, [rsp + 0x40]
call fill_output
mov rax, [rsp + 0x58]
mov rcx, [rsp + 0x68]

Here disp 0x18 0x28 --stack --all finds the two accesses relative to the explicit anchor rsp+0x40. An individual match shows that anchor, the matched field offset and the address of the instruction establishing the anchor. disp 0x58 --stack still finds the literal frame displacement.

Stack-pointer changes are normalized to entry RSP coordinates. An anchor must be established on every known incoming path before an access; conflicting or unknown frame coordinates suppress relative matching while literal searches remain available. Indexed LEA instructions do not establish constant anchors. The address-forming LEA itself matches relative offset zero under --lea.

For relative --all matches, every requested offset must be supported by the same normalized anchor. Offsets from different anchors are not combined to claim one matching buffer. Multiple interpretations of an instruction do not inflate instruction counts. Full anchor groups are ranked before raw matches.

An explicit address is evidence for an offset relationship, not proof of a source-level structure, object bounds or a callee's writes. Anchor matches are reported as candidates. This option does not infer aggregate types or sizes.

Negative frame displacements use the same 64-bit representation as other displacement queries. For [rbp - 0x20], use:

Command
xref -b app.elf disp 0xffffffffffffffe0 --stack

--stack currently applies to disp; find --disp keeps its existing literal-displacement matching and does not accept this flag.

Preserve residual labels and gotos

Command
xref -b app.elf c 0x1000 --goto
xref -b app.elf c 0x1000 --goto --fields --out out-functions
xref -b app.elf slice 0x1000 --to 0x1013 --goto
xref -b app.elf dump --out out-modules --goto

The default renderer restructures residual forward jumps with local skip_* flags when possible. --goto preserves those residual jumps as goto L_<addr>; and destination labels. Ordinary if/else, loops and switches remain structured. This is a display choice for the same recovered function; it does not improve instruction coverage or prove that the reconstruction is correct.

Use --fields independently of --goto. The mode also applies to each file written by c --out or dump. In a backward slice, retained transfers must keep their destinations so the displayed control flow remains self-contained.

The commands above illustrate the syntax; addresses depend on the input binary.

Restrict pseudo-C to paths reaching an address

Command
xref -b app.elf c 0x1000 --only-paths-to 0x1050
xref -b app.elf c 0x1000 --only-paths-to 0x1050 --goto

xref c FN --only-paths-to ADDR emits pseudo-C containing only basic blocks that can reach ADDR (an instruction address inside FN) plus the statements those blocks need, with elided regions marked by a one-line comment (/* ... */). Unrelated branches and trailing blocks that cannot reach ADDR are omitted. If ADDR is outside FN or unreachable from the entry block, the command reports a clear error. Blocks are kept whole: the statement for ADDR carries /* @xref_slice_target */, and statements after it in the same basic block are still shown. Switch arms and labels that lead only to pruned code stay as /* ... */ stubs so every emitted label is defined.
